answer_text:
Great, I now have plenty of information to give a thorough and well-cited answer. Here's a comprehensive breakdown of why animated shows tend to look better over time:

---

## Why Animated Shows Look Better Over Time

There are several interconnected reasons — covering budget, technology, talent, and workflow — that explain why animated series often improve visually as they continue airing.

---

### 1. 🎨 The Animators Get Better at Their Craft

One of the most fundamental reasons is simply that the artists grow more skilled over time. While a show's style may remain largely the same, the creatives working on it refine their skills, adding shading, sharper lines, and other elements that make the quality appear much improved. Sometimes, the style of an animation studio takes a while to mature into a particular form. Technology advances, which requires training and mastery, and budgets can change at the drop of a hat.

---

### 2. 💰 Bigger Budgets as the Show Becomes a Hit

When a show becomes successful, networks and studios are more willing to invest in it. Animated shows have seen an uptick in production costs over the last 20 years. Some shows amp up their animation consistency and choreography in later seasons — and this is directly due to the bigger budget for those later seasons.

Streaming services like Netflix, Crunchyroll, and Hulu have raised the bar for animation quality, often commissioning premium seasons with extended runtimes and higher budgets. When a show moves to a streaming platform — or gains a cult following that demands higher quality — the pressure to upgrade intensifies.

---

### 3. 🖥️ Advances in Technology

Shifts in animation quality sometimes reflect intentional upgrades in tools, software, or creative vision. Over time, studios adopt new technologies — such as digital ink-and-paint systems, 3D-assisted animation, or AI-powered tweening — that allow for smoother motion and richer textures.

For older TV shows, many started out being hand-drawn before being updated and created digitally. Some other animation techniques have also become more prominent and resulted in a multitude of styles that creators employ when making a series. For example, *The Simpsons* switched to digital ink and paint in Season 14, replacing traditional cels.

---

### 4. 📺 The Shift to HD Broadcasting

Simply changing broadcast formats can force a quality upgrade. The early seasons of *Family Guy* were considerably rougher compared to the sleek, crisp look of the show today. In fact, backgrounds were so rushed that some buildings were only distinguishable by their signs. The improvements came when the show jumped to HD format, which necessitated clearer details.

---

### 5. 👥 Changes in Creative Personnel and Studios

The creative team behind an animated series — including directors, lead animators, and character designers — plays a pivotal role in maintaining consistent quality. When key personnel leave due to contract expirations, creative differences, or new opportunities, the show's visual tone can shift dramatically.

Bringing in a new, more experienced studio can also be a major boost. Season 3 of Netflix's *Castlevania* saw improved animation after bringing in Frederator Studios and Powerhouse Animation, which invested in higher frame rates and cinematic choreography.

---

### 6. ⏳ More Time to Develop a Consistent Vision

Early in a show's run, the team is still figuring out the "look" and feel. Season 1 of *The Simpsons* was a bit more stabilized and refined than the Tracey Ullman shorts, and noticeably improved in quality over the course of the season. By Season 2, most of the character designs had been standardized, there were fewer awkward-looking shots, and the animation was much more consistent.

Animation changes in your favorite cartoons sometimes happen so steadily that you forget how dramatically different they used to look in the pilot.

---

### 7. 🎬 "Animation Bumps" for Special Moments

Even within a single season, animation quality can spike for big moments. These improvements can extend to more detailed backgrounds, improved colorwork, more impressive dynamic effects such as fire and water, and integration of CGI. Creators usually put this into practice for pivotal episodes or sequences — generally season openers, season finales, and any cinematic moments or action scenes.

---

### In Summary

The improvement in visual quality over a show's run is rarely due to a single cause. It's typically a combination of **the team gaining experience**, **larger budgets unlocked by ratings success**, **new animation technologies**, **HD broadcasting standards**, and **better-staffed studios**. More than half the time, the shifts in animation style are for the better and excite fans with better production quality.
